text: C2 holds up a picture frame with ‘Scene 6’ on the back
speaker: C2

text: Scene 6
speaker: C2

text: C2 turns the frame round to reveal a picture of a hotel parlour
speaker: C2

text: A room at the Bristol
speaker: C4/2

text: Basil Hallward was shown into a little private room at the Bristol. Lord Henry waited, eager to speak to his friend.
speaker: C4

text: I suppose you have heard the news, Basil?
speaker: Lord H

text: Nothing about politics, I hope! There is hardly a single person in the House of Common worth painting, though many of them would be the better for a little whitewashing.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian Gray is engaged to be married,
speaker: Lord H

text: Dorian engaged to be married! Impossible! To whom?
speaker: Basil

text: To some little actress or other.
speaker: Lord H

text: I can't believe it.  Dorian is far too sensible.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian is far too wise not to do foolish things now and then.
speaker: Lord H

text: I hope the girl is good, Harry.  I don't want to see Dorian tied to some vile creature.
speaker: Basil

text: Oh, she is better than good--she is beautiful. Dorian says she is beautiful, and he is not often wrong about things of that kind.  We are to see her to-night.
speaker: Lord H

text: But do you approve of it, Harry?
speaker: Basil

text: I never approve, or disapprove, of anything now. We are not sent into the world to air our moral prejudices.  I never take any notice of what common people say, and I never interfere with what charming people do. I hope that Dorian Gray will make this girl his wife, passionately adore her for six months, and then suddenly become fascinated by someone else. He would be a wonderful study.
speaker: Lord H

text: You don’t mean a word of all that Harry.
speaker: Basil

text: I mean everything I have said - But here is Dorian himself.  He will tell you more than I can.
speaker: Lord H

text: My dear Harry, my dear Basil, you must both congratulate me. I have never been so happy.
speaker: Dorian

text: Come, you will tell us how it all came about.
speaker: Lord H

text: After I left you yesterday evening, Harry, I went down to the theatre.  Sibyl was playing Rosalind. You should have seen her!  When she came on in her boy's clothes, she was perfectly wonderful. After the performance was over, I went behind and spoke to her.  My lips moved towards hers. We kissed each other. Of course, our engagement is a secret.  She has not even told her own mother. I don't know what my guardians will say.  I don't care.  I shall be of age in less than a year, and then I can do what I like.
speaker: Dorian

text: At what particular point did you mention the word marriage, Dorian?
speaker: Lord H

text: My dear Harry, I did not make any formal proposal.  I told her that I loved her, and she said she was not worthy to be my wife.  Not worthy!  Why, the whole world is nothing to me compared with her.
speaker: Dorian

text: Women are wonderfully practical - much more practical than we are. In situations of that kind we often forget to say anything about marriage, and they always remind us.
speaker: Lord H

text: When you see Sibyl Vane, you will feel that the man who could wrong her would a beast without a heart. Her trust makes me faithful, her belief makes me good.  When I am with her, I regret all that you have taught me and try to forget you and all your wrong, fascinating, poisonous, delightful theories.
speaker: Dorian

text: And those are …?
speaker: Lord H

text: Oh, your theories about life, your theories about love, your theories about pleasure.  All your theories, in fact, Harry.
speaker: Dorian

text: Pleasure is the only thing worth having a theory about. Pleasure is Nature’s test, her sign of approval. When we are happy, we are always good, but when we are good, we are not always happy.
speaker: Lord H

text: Ah! but what do you mean by good?
speaker: Basil

text: To be good is to be in harmony with one's self.  Discord is to be forced to be in harmony with others.
speaker: Lord H

text: Harry, you are dreadful!  I don't know why I like you so much.
speaker: Dorian

text: You will always like me, Dorian.
speaker: Lord H

text: Let us go down to the theatre.  When Sibyl comes on the stage you will have a new ideal of life.  She will represent something to you that you have never known.
speaker: Dorian

text: I have known everything but I am always ready for a new emotion.  Your wonderful girl may thrill me.  I love acting.  It is so much more real than life.  Let us go.
speaker: Lord H
